checks: Checked source §3 and retained its raw baseline constants. The dominated marginal constraints are weakly closed by nonnegative continuous tests; m≤min(a,c) gives a scaled product and compact supports give tightness.

For fixed unit direction, a moving through-mark closed pullback is eventually contained in the fixed η-enlarged closed pullback. Portmanteau followed by continuity from above handles charged cap boundaries. The same bound applies to the baseline, and the infimum over directions is upper semicontinuous.

Finite attainment upgrades an infeasible threshold W+ε to the strict upper bound by the compact finite intersection property. The downward closure of all finite payoff vectors is closed and convex. A supporting normal at its diagonal maximum has nonnegative coordinates and normalizes to a probability, yielding the exact finite dual.

Every full-menu fixed-center optimizer has all listed cap values at least W. The finite dual optimum is less than W+ε, so the weighted partial cost shortfall is less than ε after canceling the baseline.

overlap.comparison: Joint upper semicontinuity proof for prescribed full probability couplings. Here the weakly closed capacity constraints permit both endpoint marginals to vary.

The separation argument transfers, but the accepted statement optimizes over all full couplings of the prescribed median marginals. The trimmed subset has a fixed Lebesgue baseline and dominated, freely selected endpoint marginals.
Covers fixed-point attainment for the trimmed family in continuous dimension one. It does not give arbitrary-dimensional joint attainment or the finite dual on the varying partial marginals.

review_method: Independent cold proof read, source-locator comparison, predecessor proof comparison, and exact arithmetic replay where relevant.
summary: The feasible partial transport problem attains its joint optimum, and finite cap menus give the claimed attained dual and approximation.
